title: Ketkä: asking and answering about several people
focus: Ketkä asks which people or who several people are. Ketkä te olette? — Me olemme opettajia.
targetSkills: Ketkä: asking and answering about several people
prerequisiteSkills: Kuka: asking and answering about one person

exercises.prompt: Choose the question meaning “Who are you?”  Address a group (te).
exercises.explanation: Plural means more than one in this grammatical pattern. Ketkä asks which people or who several people are. Use plural olla forms: Ketkä te olette? (“Who are you?” addressed to a group). The complete question means “Who are you”.
requiredSkills: Ketkä: asking and answering about several people
exercises.targetSkill: Ketkä: asking and answering about several people

sentenceExplanation.pattern: question asking a person's or thing's identity + subject (who or what this sentence is about) + verb (the action or state)

parts.role: question asking a person's or thing's identity
parts.formation: Kuka has the irregular plural basic form ketkä.

parts.role: subject (who or what this sentence is about)
parts.formation: Te addresses more than one person in these dialogues.

parts.role: verb (the action or state)
parts.formation: Olla has the plural you-form olette: ole- + -tte.

optionFeedback.Ketkä te olette?: Plural means more than one in this grammatical pattern. Ketkä asks which people or who several people are. Use plural olla forms: Ketkä te olette? (“Who are you?” addressed to a group). The complete question means “Who are you”.
optionFeedback.Kuka te olette?: Kuka asks who a person is or who acts. The requested question is “Ketkä te olette?”
optionFeedback.Mitkä te olette?: Mitkä selects several things. The requested question is “Ketkä te olette?”

exercises.prompt: Answer “Ketkä me olemme?”: choose “You are Anna and Mikko.” Address a group (te).
exercises.explanation: Plural means more than one in this grammatical pattern. When a group is addressed as te, its reply uses me olemme (“we are”). When both speakers mean another group, keep he ovat (“they are”). Profession words describing the members normally take the plural partitive: opettajia (“teachers”). The complete profession forms are provided here. In a role game, Ketkä me olemme? (“Who are we?”) receives Te olette… (“You are…” addressed to the group). The complete reply means “You are Anna and Mikko”.
requiredSkills: Ketkä: asking and answering about several people
exercises.targetSkill: Ketkä: asking and answering about several people

sentenceExplanation.pattern: subject (who or what this sentence is about) + verb (the action or state) + identity or category given after olla + connector joining the two names + identity or category given after olla

parts.role: subject (who or what this sentence is about)
parts.formation: He refers to other people; this is Finnish plural he.

parts.role: verb (the action or state)
parts.formation: Olla has the irregular plural third-person form ovat.

parts.role: identity or category given after olla
parts.formation: Anna is a person's name and keeps its basic form as a subject or identity.

parts.role: connector joining the two names
parts.formation: Ja links the names without changing their forms.

parts.role: identity or category given after olla
parts.formation: Liisa is a person's name and keeps its basic form here.

answerDiagnostics.explanation: Use the requested plural person: me olemme, te olette or he ovat. A reply addressing the original speakers uses te olette; a group speaking about itself uses me olemme. The requested reply is “He ovat Anna ja Liisa.”
